To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the T lymphocyte subpopulations and the TCR gene rearrangements are abnormal in some patients.
the distribution of T cell subsets in the peripheral blood of patients with common variable immune deficiency (CVD) is heterogeneous.
the percentage of CD4+ cells bearing CD45RA is reduced in patients with CVID, and that the T cell antigen receptors of the patients with CVID are polyclonal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunological abnormalities of patients with common variable immune deficiency.
the immunoregulatory mechanisms that may be defective in patients with CVID, and we have demonstrated abnormalities of the T cell subpopulation and T cell receptor in some patients with CVID.
the immunological abnormalities of patients with CVI and their possible relationship to the clinical features of this disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence for an intrinsic defect of the T lymphocytes of patients with CVI, but that there may be a quantitative and qualitative abnormality of the T lymphocyte repertoire.
there is no single abnormality in T cell subpopulation or TCR rearrangement which is common to all patients with CVI.
the T lymphocyte abnormalities in CVI are variable and complex, but do not appear to be associated with an abnormality of TCR gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with CVI are not likely to have a monoclonal expansion of T cells and that the abnormalities seen in T cell subpopulatios may be due to defects in the regulation of T cell development.
T cell heterogeneity in CVI may be related to the abnormality in T cell regulation of immunoglobulins.
T lymphocyte regulation may be abnormal in patients with CVID.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T cells are heterogeneous in patients with CVId and the distribution of T cells is different in different individuals.
T cell heterogeneity exists in patients with CVID, and that the T cells in these patients have a polyclonally patterned TCR gene rearrangements.
the T cells in patients with CVID are not clonally expanded, which is in contrast to the T cell expansion seen in patients with other forms of immunodeficiency.
